title: European Pear: Ancient Pear Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: An orchard tree nobody plants to be looked at. The oldest pear in the Netherlands has fed an almshouse jelly pot since it was planted in 1638.
intro: Nobody planted these to be looked at. A pear is an orchard tree, grown for fruit and grubbed out when it stops paying, so an old one is something somebody chose not to replace. The oldest is in The Hague, planted in 1638 in the courtyard of an almshouse for women of unblemished character, and the residents have been turning its hard little juttepeers into jelly for close to four centuries. Helsinki's is the last survivor of a manor orchard and is reckoned the tallest and oldest pear in Finland. Two have won national votes. Slovakia's pink-fleshed pear at Bošáca, about 200 years old, took the country's Tree of the Year in 2015, and the Czech Republic elected a lone pear in a field near Mrákotín in 2023, the one a folk song says stands in the open field.
